criteria.note: I imported warp_ios_runner.py and drove run() with my own hand-written fake driver. A happy journey (launch/expect_label/tap/type/wait/expect_text/state) returned passed True with every step ok, so the CLI path returns 0. A journey asserting an absent label returned passed False, named the failing step exactly (1:expect_label), captured a FAILURE screenshot via the driver seam, stopped at the first failure (the later state was not recorded), and the CLI path returns 1. The steps and lifecycle re-drives run through a driver seam so no simulator is needed.

process_death reads a launch token before terminate and after relaunch and fails if unchanged. My stubborn fake whose terminate is a no-op (token stays the same) produced passed False with detail 'launch token unchanged ... not a real restart' - the vacuous pass is prevented in the tested scenario. background_foreground and appearance both re-assert the recovery_assertion: with a good recovery they pass, with a bad one they fail naming 'after background_foreground' / 'after appearance'. A brittle recovery after process_death fails naming the re-drive and the mismatch. Only process_death, background_foreground, appearance are offered (rotation and network loss correctly absent).

A journey declaring three profiles driven by a fake covering one returned passed False with matrix_missing listing BOTH uncovered profiles. A single declared+covered profile passed with no matrix_missing. The matrix failure is applied at the end and cannot be masked by all-passing steps (I confirmed steps were all ok yet the run still failed on the missing profiles).

The selftest iOS block uses a FakeIosDriver with no simulator, mirrors the Android block, and covers happy path, failing-assertion-exit-1-named-with-screenshot, no-op-process-death-caught, and uncovered-profile-fails. I reran python3 scripts/selftest.py (284 passed, 0 failed) and bash test_ios_runner.sh (pass exit 0, fail exit 1, rc 0). To prove the tests are not tautological I copied the runner to /tmp and applied five regressions (disable token-change check, drop the FAILURE screenshot, drop the matrix_missing fail, make assertions always pass, swallow the failing step); every mutation flipped the corresponding selftest expectation to failing, so each case genuinely catches its regression.

Case-insensitive grep for bcengi/dejitech/travelpass/workpass/agentpass/coreconnect/onesim/mvne/dmitry/tripdesk/daybook/stripe/hubspot over the runner, fixtures, wrapper, and README returned zero matches. No U+2014 or U+2013 in any added file; the only double-hyphen anywhere in the added content is the legitimate simctl JSON list flag inside a code argument list (code, not prose), and the capabilities ios line has none. Both .warp/capabilities.yaml and plugin/templates/.warp/capabilities.yaml are byte-identical (sha256 44e67ceacb99608e431755cf7f5055a78c589a0c48e9506d1f407f383614784d) and declare ios_simulator_driving status: reference, never mechanical. verify.sh reported docs, secret, lint, and template-sync all green.

findings.text: The process_death launch-token restart proof is conditioned on a prior launch having set a baseline token. I constructed a malformed journey that declares process_death but has NO launch step: with a stubborn no-op-terminate driver it passed vacuously (before token was None so the unchanged-token check was skipped, and the fresh relaunch satisfied the recovery assertion). This is not reachable by any shipped fixture or by any AC2 scenario (every fixture and selftest case launches the app first, and the tested no-op-after-launch case IS caught), so it does not refute AC2; it is a note that the real-restart invariant is only enforced once a launch has established a baseline token.

summary: I independently reran everything at HEAD 8443c080aa184053ef1a71edb2d811ce7b878676 and confirmed it is HEAD. I recomputed the manifest proof_digest with .warp/validate.py and got sha256:d37227a328d2c1a1, matching the manifest. verify.sh printed GATE: GREEN bound to 8443c08 with 0 undeclared, and scripts/selftest.py reported 284 passed, 0 failed. I read warp_ios_runner.py in full and exercised its control logic against my own hand-written fake drivers (not the repo fakes): AC1 (journey sequencing, exit 0 all-pass, exit 1 with the failing step named and a FAILURE screenshot), AC2 (process_death proven by a launch-token change, no-op terminate caught, background_foreground and appearance re-assert, brittle recovery names the re-drive), and AC3 (partial matrix fails naming every uncovered profile) all held under adversarial inputs. For AC4 I applied five regressions to a /tmp copy and confirmed each is caught by the selftest, so the tests are not tautological. For AC5 the added content is fully generic, dash-clean, and both capabilities files are byte-identical with status reference. The honesty claim holds: the runner never fakes a simulator run, the live path fails loud on this Linux host (FileNotFoundError xcrun, exit 1), the manifest's operational evidence documents real command runs (selftest, wrapper, loud-fail) and explicitly disclaims a live-simulator run, and required_evidence [unit] is the honest choice. One note-level edge (process_death without a prior launch step skips the restart proof) does not refute any AC and is unreachable by the shipped fixtures. Verdict: pass_with_notes.
